title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
abstract: arXiv:2611.29363v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%

translated_title: 是学习器还是汇总特征的极限？在KASCADE和GRAPES-3上审计大气簇射阵列的机器学习能量重建
translated_abstract: 宇宙线阵列的机器学习能量估计器通常在少数拟合的簇射参数上训练，而非台站原始信号。当其分辨率不再提升时，标准诊断方法无法判断是更好的模型会带来帮助，还是汇总特征已经耗尽了信息。我们采用一种五步审计流程，将训练好的模型与一个与学习器无关的估计值进行比较——该估计值给出汇总特征所允许的最低误差（即其平方损失下的贝叶斯风险，称为下限），同时测试哪些输入能增加信息，并标记出仅由拟合计算得出的输入。我们将该方法应用于使用三种强相互作用模型（QGSJET-II-04、EPOS-LHC和SIBYLL-2.3d）的公开KASCADE模拟、13,848,509个实测KASCADE事件以及模拟的GRAPES-3事件。结果表明，在10^16 eV以下的已知能量区间内，基于九个重建特征的梯度提升方法在所有估计器设置下都处于估计下限的2.2%以内，因此更强的模型容量预计不会带来超过约2%的提升。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种五步审计方法，通过将机器学习模型的误差与汇总特征的贝叶斯风险下限进行比较，证明KASCADE和GRAPES-3阵列在10^16 eV以下的能量重建已接近由拟合簇射参数所决定的理论极限，进一步改进模型的空间不超过约2%。
en_tdlr: This work introduces a five-step audit that benchmarks machine-learning energy estimators against the learner-independent Bayes-risk floor of fitted shower-parameter summaries, demonstrating that KASCADE and GRAPES-3 energy reconstruction below 10^16 eV is already within about 2% of the information limit, leaving little room for model improvements.
